content.text:
required: false
  extensions:
    description: 'pi extensions to load: npm package specs or paths relative to the workspace, one per line or comma-separated. pi extensions contribute the model providers they register; packages with a pi-durable extension (pi.durable in package.json) add their tools to the conversation. npm packages are installed into a temp directory without lifecycle scripts. Extensions run inside the action with the job''s permissions and environment.'
    required: false
    default: ''
  trust_project:
    description: 'Let pi-durable extensions trust the repository: load and run its own configuration (such as .pi/ files). Only for repositories whose code you would run anyway; anyone who can open a PR can change those files.'
    required: false
    default: 'false'
  agent_dir:
    description: 'Agent directory (user-level state) for pi-durable extensions, relative to the workspace; a fresh temp directory under RUNNER_TEMP when empty'
    required: false
    default: ''
  worktree_snapshots:
    description: 'Save the files pi leaves uncommitted with the thread (on refs/pi/worktrees/<number>) and restore them at the start of the next run'
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  worktree_snapshot_exclude:
    description: 'Globs of untracked files never to save in a working-tree snapshot, one per line or comma-separated (for example .env*, *.pem, *.key, id_rsa*). Ignored files are never saved'
    required: false
    default: ''
  prompt_template:
    description: 'Custom prompt template with placeholder variables'
    required: false
  output_mode:
    description: 'How to deliver results: comment (post to issue/PR) or output (set action outputs only)'
    required: false
    default: 'comment'
  prompt:
    description: 'Direct prompt for the agent (requires output_mode: output when no issue/PR context is available)'
    required: false
    default: ''
  pr_number:
    description: 'Pull request number to load explicitly (useful for workflow_dispatch)'
    required: false
    default: ''

outputs:
  response:
    description: 'The agent response text when output_mode is output'
    value: ${{ steps.run-pi-action.outputs.response }}
  success:
    description: 'Whether the agent succeeded (true/false) when output_mode is output'
    value: ${{ steps.run-pi-action.outputs.success }}

runs:

docs/extensions.md-97-pi-durable extensions run in the process of pi-action. Thus, pi-action also sets `GH_TOKEN` and the git identity in its own environment when it loads such an extension. See [Security](security.md#the-agents-github-token-and-git-identity).

docs/extensions.md:99:### `trust_project`
docs/extensions.md-100-
docs/extensions.md:101:`trust_project` (default `false`) tells the extension that it can load and run the configuration of the repository. For pit, this is `.pi/pit.json` and `.pi/functions`.
docs/extensions.md-102-
docs/extensions.md:103:Anyone who can push a branch or open a pull request can change those files. Set `trust_project: true` only for repositories whose code you already run. Do not set it in workflows that run on pull requests from people you do not trust.
docs/extensions.md-104-
docs/extensions.md-105-## Questions on GitHub
docs/extensions.md-106-
docs/extensions.md-107-A tool can ask its user a question with `ui.confirm`, `ui.select`, or `ui.input`. (pit asks with its `ui.*` globals, and also when it promotes a function to the project.) pi-action posts the question as a comment on the issue or pull request, and **the run ends**. An answer starts a new run, which continues the thread.
docs/extensions.md-108-
docs/extensions.md-109-pi-action does not wait for the answer, because people can take hours or days to answer.
docs/extensions.md-110-
docs/extensions.md-111-### The sequence
docs/extensions.md-112-
docs/extensions.md-113-1. The tool calls `ui.ask` of pi-action. pi-action posts the question and returns its URL immediately. pit stops the program (the calls that it made before the question keep their effects) and ends the turn with "Question posted: ...".
docs/extensions.md-114-2. The run ends quietly. pi-action posts no `pi Response` comment. The log tells which question pi waits for. pi-action saves the thread as usual.
docs/extensions.md-115-3. A person answers: they tick a box (an `issue_comment` `edited` event), or they reply `/answer ...` (an `issue_comment` `created` event). The answer starts a new run on the same thread.

docs/security.md-73-- Pin npm versions (`name@1.2.3`) or git refs (`github:owner/repo#v1.2.3`).
docs/security.md-74-- Prefer a copy that you reviewed and committed to the repository (a path).
docs/security.md:75:- Keep `trust_project` off, unless you trust all people who can change the repository. See [Extensions](extensions.md#trust_project).
docs/security.md-76-
docs/security.md-77-## Thread contents are visible
docs/security.md-78-
docs/security.md-79-pi-action stores the full conversation in `refs/pi/threads/<number>`, also the output of tools. It stores the files that pi leaves uncommitted in `refs/pi/worktrees/<number>`, also untracked files that git does not ignore. All people who can read the repository can read these refs. The workflow log shows the arguments of each tool call and the last 30 lines of its output (see [The workflow log](how-it-works.md#the-workflow-log)); GitHub masks registered secrets in the log, but not in the refs. pi-action stops the runner from running workflow commands (such as `::error::` or `::add-mask::`) in the text of pi and in the output of tools. Keep secrets away from the agent, as for all CI jobs. Make git ignore files with secrets, or list them in `worktree_snapshot_exclude`. See [Durable threads](threads.md#read-a-thread) and [Working-tree continuity](threads.md#working-tree-continuity).
